page: Microsoft Azure D128s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance features 128 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the D128s_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core scores rank in the top tier, supported by a massive 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only cached small block transfers reaching 8778.99 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 508.63 GB/sec. The processor's cryptographic and vector extensions contribute to top-tier Passmark CPU extended instructions and database operations scores.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D128s_v6 offers a high-density resource profile suitable for enterprise-scale workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of high memory bandwidth, rapid multi-threaded decompression, and strong LLM inference speeds makes this server well-suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving at high throughput, multi-threaded software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
